name: Windsurf
summary: An editor built around a cascading agent that keeps watching your edits instead of waiting for a prompt.
description:
Windsurf's pitch is that the agent should notice what you are doing: it follows your recent edits and terminal output, so the next suggestion arrives with context you did not have to type. In practice that reads as fewer "explain what I meant" round trips on medium-sized tasks, and the preview-and-accept step is there before anything lands in a file.

It is a full editor replacement, so the adoption cost is migration rather than a plugin install, and enterprise teams usually stop at that sentence. As with every agentic editor, the useful question is not how smart it looks in a demo but how cheap its mistakes are to spot.
